title: Companies Act, 2013 — Section 174 (Quorum for meetings of Board)

content.overview: Section 174 provides that the quorum for a meeting of the Board of Directors of a company shall be one-third of its total strength or two directors, whichever is higher, and the participation of the directors by video conferencing or other audio-visual means shall also be counted for the purposes of quorum under this section. Interested directors are not counted for quorum on the item in which they are interested. If the number of continuing directors is reduced below the quorum, the continuing directors may act only for the purpose of increasing the number of directors to that fixed for the quorum, or of summoning a general meeting of the company.
content.glance: Quorum = higher of one-third of total strength or two directors; video participation counts where permitted; interested directors excluded from quorum on their item; continuing directors below quorum may only fill numbers or call a GM.
content.study: The quorum for a meeting of the Board of Directors of a company shall be one-third of its total strength or two directors, whichever is higher, and the participation of the directors by video conferencing or by other audio-visual means shall also be counted for the purposes of quorum under this sub-section. Where at any time the number of interested directors exceeds or is equal to two-thirds of the total strength of the Board of Directors, the number of directors who are not interested directors and present at the meeting, being not less than two, shall be the quorum during such time. If the number of continuing directors is reduced below the quorum fixed by the Act or the articles, the continuing directors may act for the purpose of increasing the number of directors to that fixed for the quorum, or of summoning a general meeting of the company, and for no other purpose. Current-law framing: compute one-third vs two; exclude interested directors on the item; apply the reduced-board rule if numbers fall below quorum.

sections.heading: Basic Quorum
sections.body: One-third of total strength or two directors, whichever is higher.

sections.heading: Video Participation
sections.body: Directors participating by video conferencing or other audio-visual means count toward quorum where the rules allow the item to be dealt with that way.

sections.heading: Interested Directors
sections.body: An interested director is not counted for quorum on the matter in which he is interested. If interested directors are two-thirds or more of total strength, quorum is the non-interested directors present, being not less than two.

sections.heading: Below Quorum
sections.body: Continuing directors reduced below quorum may act only to increase numbers to the quorum figure or to summon a general meeting.

examples.title: Six-director board
examples.body: A board of six directors needs the higher of one-third (two) or two — so two directors form quorum, subject to interest exclusions.

examples.title: Interested majority
examples.body: On a related-party item, four of six directors are interested. Quorum for that item is the non-interested directors present, being not less than two.

hypotheticals.question: Can a single director validly hold a board meeting if articles say so?
hypotheticals.analysis: No. Section 174 sets a statutory floor of two directors (or one-third if higher). Articles cannot reduce the statutory quorum below that floor.

distinctions.title: Board quorum (s. 174) vs board meetings (s. 173)
distinctions.left: How many directors must be present
distinctions.right: How often the board must meet and notice rules

misconceptions.trap: Interested directors still count toward the overall meeting quorum for every item.
misconceptions.correction: On the item in which a director is interested, that director is not counted for quorum.

questionsAndAnswers.question: How should a Section 174 problem be analysed?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: I. Compute one-third vs two. II. Apply interest exclusions. III. Check video participation if used. IV. Apply reduced-board rule if relevant. V. Conclude.

questionsAndAnswers.question: What should submissions contain?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: Board strength; attendance; interest facts; precise relief.

examTips: Interested directors out of quorum on their item.
Below quorum → only fill numbers or call GM.

learningObjectives: State the board quorum rule under s. 174.

enhancement.definition: Section 174 fixes board quorum as the higher of one-third of total strength or two directors, with rules for video participation, interested directors, and boards reduced below quorum.
enhancement.legalPrinciple: Board decisions require a minimum presence so that collective deliberation is real, subject to interest-based exclusions.
essentialIngredients: Higher of one-third of total strength or two directors
Interested directors not counted on their item
Below quorum: only increase numbers or summon GM
enhancement.detailedExplanation: Section 174 is the quorum companion to the meeting-frequency rules in s. 173.
enhancement.problemApplication: Compute quorum; apply interest rules; test validity of the meeting.
